assets.title: Five assets that can carry Perfect New Mexico.
assets.line: Each is owned by New Mexicans today and can carry a standard of living.

items.name: The Land Grant Permanent Fund
items.line: Built since 1912 from royalties on state trust land; it pays for public schools and early childhood every year.

items.name: The Severance Tax Permanent Fund
items.line: Saved from oil and gas taxes not needed for bonds, and paid into the general fund.

items.name: The trust land
items.line: Surface acres held in trust, with 13 million mineral acres, earning for schools and other beneficiaries in every county.

items.name: The Tax Stabilization Reserve
items.line: The State’s reserve for a fall in revenue, managed by the State Investment Council.

items.name: The people
items.line: New Mexicans on 1 July 2025: the asset every other asset serves.

solutions.title: Solutions for Perfect New Mexico, in order.
solutions.line: Reading first: the State already endows childcare, and reading is where the gap is widest.

items.challenge: computed:reading of fourth graders read at the NAEP Proficient level in 2024, against computed:reading_us nationally.
items.advises: Tie part of the early childhood fund’s growth to reading: an outcome contract that pays providers for measured gains by third grade, starting in McKinley County.

items.challenge: computed:poverty of New Mexicans lived below the poverty line in 2025; 33.2% in McKinley County (2020–2024).
items.advises: Invest a share of the Severance Tax Permanent Fund in New Mexico enterprises that hire in the poorest counties, with the returns shared with the fund.

items.challenge: 4,683 New Mexicans had no home on one night in January 2025.
items.advises: Lease state trust land for homes near jobs: ground rents go to the trust beneficiaries, and investors are repaid as households are housed.

solutions.hold: Phase 3, hold the line: food (computed:food of households food insecure) and health (computed:uninsured uninsured), with water and energy measured next.

intelligence.title: A delayed SNAP bill, and the time to cut it.
intelligence.line: From October 2027 every state pays part of its SNAP food benefits unless at least 94 of every 100 dollars are paid exactly right. AI that checks every case before it is paid can shrink that bill.
intelligence.bill_label: a year in SNAP benefits once the delayed start ends, at the full 15% share

facts.label: of SNAP dollars paid in error, 2025
start for states at or above 13.33%; then up to 15% of benefits

intelligence.advises: Use the delay. The aim is under 6%, where the State pays nothing; falling only part of the way ends the delay and brings a 15% bill forward. Fund AI case review from the early childhood model, with quarterly audits for underpayments as well as overpayments.
